channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: This Blue Whale Population Grew 1,000% Since the End of Antarctic Whaling
item.description: Antarctic blue whales have grown from 418 to about 4,000 since whaling there stopped in 1973. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Rhino Dung Paper Is How This Family Makes Money and Protects These Amazing Animals
item.description: A family turns rhino dung into paper, so nearby villagers now earn from rhinos instead of clashing with them. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Every Tuesday, This Chef Cooks for 100 People in Need Using Random Food Bank Ingredients
item.description: A Toronto chef cooks a scratch meal for 100 people every Tuesday from whatever the food bank has. How you can help: Ask your local food bank whether it needs volunteer cooks or kitchen help. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
item.description: CERN physicists found the first evidence of a particle decay they had hunted for 40 years. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Montreal Is Harnessing Soothing Ocean Sounds to Combat Traffic Noise
item.description: A Montreal pocket park plays ocean sounds to soften traffic noise, and visitors find it calmer. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites
item.description: Former coal mine sites in Yorkshire are being restored as homes for amphibians and lizards. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Leave a wild corner in your garden with logs or stones for frogs and lizards. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: CAR-T therapy helps stiff person syndrome patients walk and work again
item.description: In an early Mayo Clinic trial, CAR-T therapy helped people with stiff person syndrome walk and work again. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: She Checked on Her ‘Loud’ Upstairs Neighbor, Inspiring Strangers to Raise More Than $100,000
item.description: One neighbour checked on an 87-year-old with Parkinson’s, and strangers raised over $109,000 to support her. How you can help: Knock on an older neighbour’s door this week and ask how they are doing. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Empire State Building Lit Up with Gold Marks Historic Milestone of NASA’s Voyager 1 This Week
item.description: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is still sending signals home from a full light-day away. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Over 100 Cave Bear Skeletons Found in ‘Sensational’ Discovery by Alpine Guide
item.description: An Alpine guide found a cave holding the bones of more than 100 extinct cave bears, kept safe for study. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Waterless, Hyper-Efficient Machines That Clean Clothes With Carbon Dioxide
item.description: New machines clean clothes with recycled carbon dioxide instead of water and heat. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Students Fighting to Save Poached Plant Species That Only Exists Near Their Campus
item.description: Students at Santa Clara University are working to save a poached wildflower that grows only in their valley. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Buy succulents only from nurseries that grow their own, never plants dug from the wild. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Siblings Build 430-Step ‘Sky Ladder’ for Their Mother Who Refuses to Live in the City
item.description: Siblings built a 430-step staircase up a mountain by hand so their mother can keep living in her home. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Huge experiment in biogeography’: US offshore windfarms are creating artificial reefs
item.description: US offshore windfarm foundations are turning into artificial reefs that fish and other sea life now use. Evidence: Early research. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Scientists ‘Cure’ Deadly Brain Tumors in Every Mouse Tested with New Cancer Therapy
item.description: A new immune-cell therapy cleared an aggressive childhood brain cancer in every mouse tested at UCSF. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
item.description: Physicists showed one key ingredient of superconductivity can exist at room temperature. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
item.description: Tools and fossils show early humans lived by lakes full of hippos in today’s Arabian desert. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: US homelessness decline hits its steepest one-year drop in a decade
item.description: US homelessness fell more than 6% in 2025, about 49,000 fewer people, the steepest drop in a decade. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Ask a local shelter what it needs this winter; warm socks and toiletries are common asks. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: April Surac built NeuraSensa so art adapts to the people using it
item.description: A young designer built NeuraSensa, art installations that adapt to the senses of each visitor. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind
item.description: Rooftop panels pushed solar from 1% to 28% of Pakistan’s electricity. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: West Coast’s First Ever Sea Turtle Hatchlings Released into the Pacific (LOOK)
item.description: The first olive ridley turtle hatchlings recorded on the US West Coast were saved from a storm and reached the sea. How you can help: Give marked turtle nests on beaches a wide berth and report new ones to local wildlife officers. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Algeria Returns Kindness Shown by Kansans Who Welcomed its World Cup Team with the Trip of a Lifetime
item.description: Algeria hosted the Kansas families who welcomed its World Cup team, returning their kindness with a trip. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Warren Buffett Gives Away $5.5 Billion in Thanksgiving Gift, Saying Kindness Is Priceless
item.description: Warren Buffett gave about $5.5 billion in shares to charity for Thanksgiving. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
item.description: New York’s largest electric school bus fleet now runs in a South Bronx area with high childhood asthma. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?
item.description: A Somerset farm is testing apple varieties and methods to keep cider orchards thriving as the climate shifts. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Greek coastline cleanup that turned trash into a pollution map
item.description: A Greek islet cleanup logged every item it found, turning beach rubbish into a map of pollution sources. How you can help: Join a beach or river clean and record what you find. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Animal welfare ballot measures had a strong night in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Voters in the 2026 US midterms passed several animal welfare measures by wide margins. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Farmer Finds Unknown Seeds in His Attic – and Grows an Ancient ‘Miracle’ Grain
item.description: An Italian farmer grew an ancient grain from seeds found in his attic, reviving a hardy old crop. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 30% Drop in Levels of Forever Chemicals in England’s Rivers, 49% in Fish – ‘Brilliant to See’
item.description: After bans, two forever chemicals fell about 30% in England’s rivers and nearly half in fish. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
item.description: NASA is inviting students to design parts of a permanent Moon base, with $1 million in prizes. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Deep-sea metal nodules turned out to host over 4,100 small animals, one rock holding 245. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Staten Island barbershops are offering health checks, reaching Black men who often avoid clinics. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Get your blood pressure checked; many pharmacies do it for free. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: This Tourette’s wrist device cut tics by a quarter in a UK trial
item.description: A wrist device cut tics by a quarter on average in a UK trial of 121 people with Tourette’s. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: A model suggests vitamin C with nitrate-rich meals may stop cancer-linked compounds forming in the stomach. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: Rockefeller scientists found low arginine weakens immune defences, hinting a supplement could help. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: The Euclid telescope found 31 ancient quasars, two from when the Universe was 670 million years old. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time
item.description: SpaceX caught the upper stage of Starship in mid-air, a step toward fully reusable rockets. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers spotted 2026 ED138, a large icy world beyond Pluto that may become the sixth dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is shaping tourism that asks visitors to help restore land and community. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, choose local stays and tours that keep money in the community. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Tübingen researchers found crows make visual decisions about twice as fast as humans. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: AI helped predict what a blind man with a brain implant sees, making bionic vision more precise. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A common tropical butterfly turned out to be three species, one new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A German effort that began by saving one tree is now testing moss to cool and clean city air. Evidence: Early research. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding childcare, family spaces and flexible help so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, neighbours feed each other by sharing fish, game and garden food across the community. How you can help: Share surplus garden produce or bulk food with a neighbour this week. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community and purpose through small farms. Source: The Guardian Environment.
